heading.title: Fire Skills
heading.description: Choose a fire type to learn about its structure, materials, and safety.

skills.name: Teepee Fire
skills.description: A cone-shaped fire structure that allows air to move between the sticks.
skills.imageAlt: Teepee fire structure made with kindling

details.name: Teepee Fire
details.imageAlt: Teepee fire structure made with kindling around a small fire
introduction: The teepee fire is a common way to arrange wood when starting a campfire.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A teepee fire uses small pieces of wood arranged in a cone shape around tinder. The structure leaves open spaces that allow air to reach the fire.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: This structure can be useful when starting a campfire because small pieces of wood can catch fire before larger pieces are added.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Tinder is placed in the center. Small dry sticks are placed around the tinder in a cone shape. Larger pieces of wood can be added after the fire becomes stronger.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Only build a fire where fires are allowed. Keep the area around the fire clear and never leave a burning fire unattended.

skills.name: Log Cabin Fire
skills.description: A fire structure made by stacking wood in alternating layers.
skills.imageAlt: Log cabin fire structure made with stacked wood

details.name: Log Cabin Fire
details.imageAlt: Log cabin fire structure with stacked pieces of firewood
introduction: A log cabin fire uses pieces of wood stacked in alternating layers.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: The wood is arranged in a square shape. Each layer is placed across the layer below it, similar to the walls of a small log cabin.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: This structure can be used for a campfire when a stable arrangement of firewood is wanted.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Two pieces of wood are placed parallel to each other. Another two pieces are placed across them. More layers can then be added while leaving space for air.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Use established fire areas when available. Keep water nearby and completely extinguish the fire before leaving the area.

skills.name: Lean-to Fire
skills.description: A fire structure where small sticks lean against a larger piece of wood.
skills.imageAlt: Lean-to fire structure with sticks leaning against a log

details.name: Lean-to Fire
details.imageAlt: Lean-to fire structure with small sticks leaning against a larger log
introduction: The lean-to fire uses a larger piece of wood to support smaller pieces of kindling.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A larger piece of wood is placed on the ground. Smaller sticks are leaned against it with tinder placed underneath.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: It is a simple fire structure that can provide support for small pieces of kindling while a fire is being started.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Tinder is placed next to the larger piece of wood. Small sticks lean over the tinder. More wood can be added carefully after the fire begins burning.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Never build a fire where it is prohibited. Keep the fire small and under control and completely extinguish it when finished.

skills.name: Star Fire
skills.description: A fire where long logs point toward a small burning center.
skills.imageAlt: Star fire with logs pointing toward the center

details.name: Star Fire
details.imageAlt: Star fire with logs pointing toward a burning center
introduction: A star fire places several pieces of wood around a central burning area.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: Several logs are placed on the ground with one end of each log pointing toward the center. From above, the arrangement looks like a star.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: The arrangement allows wood to be moved toward the center as the ends burn.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: A small fire is started in the center. The ends of the larger pieces of wood are positioned near the flame and can be moved inward carefully as they burn.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Keep the fire within an established fire area when possible. Never leave it unattended and completely extinguish it before leaving.

categories.name: Shelter
categories.description: Learn about simple shelters for different outdoor situations.
categories.imageAlt: Simple wooden survival shelter in a forest

heading.title: Shelter Skills
heading.description: Choose a shelter type to learn about its purpose, materials, and safety.

skills.name: Lean-to Shelter
skills.description: A simple shelter with a sloping roof.

details.name: Lean-to Shelter
details.imageAlt: Lean-to survival shelter made from branches
introduction: A lean-to is a simple outdoor shelter with a sloping roof.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A lean-to shelter has a roof that slopes from a higher support down toward the ground. The roof can be covered with available materials to provide protection.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: A lean-to can provide basic protection from wind, light rain, and direct sunlight when spending time outdoors.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: A strong horizontal support is used as the main part of the shelter. Smaller branches can lean against it to create the roof. The roof can then be covered.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Check the area before building. Avoid dead trees, unstable branches, flood areas, and other possible hazards.

skills.name: Tarp Shelter
skills.description: A lightweight shelter made using a tarp.

details.name: Tarp Shelter
details.imageAlt: Tarp survival shelter secured between trees
introduction: A tarp can be used to create a simple temporary outdoor shelter.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A tarp shelter uses a waterproof sheet supported by trees, poles, or other strong anchor points.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: It can provide temporary protection from rain, wind, or direct sunlight while outdoors.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: A tarp is secured above the ground using cord and strong anchor points. It can be angled so rainwater runs away from the sheltered area.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Make sure the shelter is securely attached. Do not place it under dead branches or in areas where water may collect.

skills.name: Debris Hut
skills.description: A basic shelter made with natural materials.
skills.imageAlt: Debris hut made from branches and forest materials

details.name: Debris Hut
details.imageAlt: Debris hut made from branches and forest materials
introduction: A debris hut is a small shelter made mainly from natural materials.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A debris hut uses branches to create a basic frame. Leaves and other dry natural materials can cover the frame.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: It can provide basic protection when a normal tent or tarp is not available.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: A strong branch forms the main support. Smaller branches are placed along the sides. Dry leaves and other debris can then cover the frame.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Check the location for hazards before building. Avoid unstable trees, falling branches, animal areas, and places that may flood.

skills.name: Snow Shelter
skills.description: A shelter designed for snowy conditions.
skills.imageAlt: Emergency survival shelter built from snow

details.name: Snow Shelter
details.imageAlt: Emergency survival shelter built from snow
introduction: Snow can sometimes be used to create temporary protection in snowy environments.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A snow shelter is a temporary structure that uses snow as part of its walls or covering. Snow can help block wind and provide insulation.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: Snow shelters are associated with cold and snowy environments where protection from wind and cold is important.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Snow is shaped or dug to create a protected space. The exact design depends on the snow, weather, location, and available equipment.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Snow shelters can collapse and poor ventilation can be dangerous. Cold-weather shelter building requires proper knowledge and careful conditions.

categories.name: Water
categories.description: Learn about collecting and preparing water outdoors.
categories.imageAlt: Water being poured into a metal cup from a water bottle

heading.title: Water Skills
heading.description: Choose a water skill to learn about its purpose, materials, and safety.

skills.name: Boiling
skills.description: Learn how boiling can help make water safer to drink.
skills.imageAlt: Water boiling in a metal camping pot

details.name: Boiling Water
details.imageAlt: Water boiling in a metal camping pot over a fire
introduction: Boiling is one method that can help make water safer to drink.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: Boiling uses high heat to kill many disease-causing microorganisms that may be present in water.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: Boiling can be used when the safety of available water is uncertain and a safe heat source is available.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: If the water is cloudy, it should first be allowed to settle and be filtered through a clean cloth when possible. The water can then be brought to a rolling boil before being allowed to cool.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Boiling does not remove every type of chemical contamination. Avoid water that may contain fuel, toxic chemicals, or other dangerous pollutants.

paragraphs.label: CDC - Making Water Safe in an Emergency

skills.name: Water Filtering
skills.description: Learn how portable filters can be used to prepare water.

details.name: Water Filtering
details.imageAlt: Portable water filter being used beside a mountain stream
introduction: Portable water filters can help remove certain contaminants from outdoor water.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: Water filtering passes water through a filter designed to remove certain particles and microorganisms.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: A portable water filter can be useful while hiking or camping when treated drinking water is not available.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Water passes through the filter before it reaches a clean container. Different filters remove different contaminants, so the manufacturer's instructions are important.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Not every filter removes viruses, chemicals, or all other contaminants. Use a filter designed for the situation and follow its instructions.

paragraphs.label: CDC - Making Water Safe in an Emergency

skills.name: Collecting Rainwater
skills.description: Learn how rainwater can be collected using a clean surface.
skills.imageAlt: Rainwater being collected from a tarp

details.name: Collecting Rainwater
details.imageAlt: Rainwater being collected from a tarp into a container
introduction: Rainwater can be collected using a clean surface and container.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: Rainwater collection means catching rain and directing it into a container for later use.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: It may provide an additional source of water when rain is available and normal water supplies are limited.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: A clean tarp or similar surface can direct falling rain toward a clean container. The collected water should be protected from additional contamination.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Rainwater is not automatically safe to drink. It can collect germs and chemicals from the air or collection surface. Treat water when necessary before drinking it.

paragraphs.label: CDC - Finding Clean Water in an Emergency

skills.name: Solar Still
skills.description: Learn how a solar still collects small amounts of water.
skills.imageAlt: Solar still using clear plastic and a collection container

details.name: Solar Still
details.imageAlt: Solar still collecting water using clear plastic and a container
introduction: A solar still uses heat, evaporation, and condensation to collect a small amount of water.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A solar still is a simple system where heat causes moisture to evaporate. The water vapor then condenses on a surface and can be collected.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: It can demonstrate one way that water can move through evaporation and condensation when sunlight is available.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Sunlight warms moisture inside a covered area. Water evaporates and reaches the cooler covering. It then condenses into droplets that can move toward a collection container.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: A small solar still may produce very little water and should not be depended on as the only source of drinking water.

categories.name: Navigation & Signaling
categories.description: Learn basic navigation and ways to signal for help.
categories.imageAlt: Compass on a map with a forest in the background

heading.title: Navigation & Signaling
heading.description: Choose a skill to learn about navigation and ways to signal for help.

skills.name: Compass
skills.description: Learn how a compass can help identify direction outdoors.

details.name: Compass
details.imageAlt: Compass being used for navigation in the wilderness
introduction: A compass is a navigation tool that helps identify direction.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A basic magnetic compass has a needle that aligns with Earth's magnetic field. This helps the user identify magnetic north and other directions.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: A compass can be useful while hiking, camping, or navigating an unfamiliar area, especially when used together with a map.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: The compass should be held flat and away from objects that may interfere with it. The needle helps identify direction, which can then be compared with a map or route.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Learn how to use a compass before depending on it outdoors. Electronic devices and some metal objects can also affect compass readings.

skills.name: Trail Markers
skills.description: Learn how trail markers can help hikers follow a route.

details.name: Trail Markers
details.imageAlt: Examples of trail markers used for outdoor navigation
introduction: Trail markers help hikers identify and follow established trails.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: Trail markers are signs, symbols, posts, or painted markings placed along established trails to help people follow a route.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: Pay attention to trail markers when hiking on marked trails, especially near turns, intersections, and changes in the route.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Hikers follow the official markings for their selected trail. A map can also help confirm the route and important locations.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Do not create or change official trail markers. Stay on established trails when required and follow signs from park or land officials.

skills.name: Signal Fire
skills.description: Learn how a visible fire or smoke can be used to signal for help.

details.name: Signal Fire
details.imageAlt: Signal fire producing visible smoke in a wilderness clearing
introduction: A signal fire may help attract attention during an emergency where fire use is safe and legally permitted.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A signal fire is intended to make a person's location more noticeable from a distance. The visible flame or smoke may attract attention.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: It may be considered during an emergency when signaling for rescue is necessary and local conditions allow a fire to be used safely.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: The main purpose is visibility. A signal should be placed where it can be noticed without creating a wildfire or another hazard.

sections.heading: Materials Needed
items: Water or another way to extinguish the fire

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Fire can spread quickly. Follow local fire restrictions and never start a fire when conditions make it unsafe. Other signaling methods should be used when fire is prohibited.

paragraphs.label: National Park Service - Wildland Fire Safety

skills.name: Ground Signals
skills.description: Learn how large ground markings can help attract rescuers.

details.name: Ground Signals
details.imageAlt: Examples of large emergency ground signals
introduction: Large visible ground markings can help make a location easier to notice from a distance.

sections.heading: What It Is
paragraphs: A ground signal is a large marking created in an open area using materials that contrast with the surrounding ground.

sections.heading: When to Use It
paragraphs: Ground signals may be useful when trying to make your location more visible to rescuers from a distance.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Materials can be arranged into a large, simple shape in a clear area. The signal should be large enough to stand out from the surrounding landscape.

safety.heading: Safety Note
paragraphs: Do not put yourself in danger while making a signal. Avoid cliffs, unstable ground, moving water, and other hazardous areas.
